findings.reason: the declared write scope cannot produce the deliverable, and the plan names no caller that threads the project to `_applies`, so a dispatched node would either stop on an out-of-scope blocker or ship a resolver nothing reaches.
findings.text: s53's deliverable is "a project lift covers every dispatch whose project matches", and its write paths are `reckon/crew/budget_lift.py`, `reckon/crew_run_commands.py`, `reckon/crew/lift_watch.py`, the skill and the new test, but a dispatch resolves its effective budget through a chain the plan never names and does not grant: `reckon/crew/routing.py:_budget_verdict` → `_config_with_effective_budget` (`routing.py:413`, session only) → `budget_group.effective_block` (`reckon/crew/budget_group.py:246`, session only) → `budget_lift.effective_budget` (`budget_lift.py:553`, signature carries `session` and no `project`) → `_governing_lift` → `_applies`. `_applies` (`budget_lift.py:1033`) reads `group` and `session` and nothing that identifies a project, so a build confined to the declared write paths cannot make a project match reach it, and every dispatch would still resolve as it does now — the project scope would parse, persist and clear without ever admitting a dispatch. The change is larger than `_applies`: `effective_budget` and `budget_group.effective_block` must take and forward a project, and `routing._budget_verdict` (which already holds `project`) must supply it; the picker's `_effective_budget_block` (`reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py:1093`) reads the same resolver and takes only `session`

findings.reason: without the project-over-global case the node's gate cannot falsify the wrong precedence, and the stated rule ships unmeasured.
findings.text: the deliverable fixes the precedence "session over project over global", but the five done-when cases measure the session-over-project arm only; nothing stands up a project lift and a global lift in force together and asserts the project one governs. Today `_governing_lift` (`reckon/crew/budget_lift.py:1000`) prefers a session lift and otherwise takes the newest by `granted_at`, so a build that adds the project match but leaves that tie-break would pass all five cases while a newer global lift silently overrides a project lift the plan says must govern
